intent: Customer (ID&V passed) wants the Oakfield PM Direct Debit stopped before Monday's £2,525 collection, refunds of the 24 Aug and 23 Sep £875 collections, and the £6.50 unarranged overdraft fee reversed.
summary: Cancel mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312 now on the customer's instruction and ask the payments team to stop/return the scheduled 28 Sep £2,525 collection (received 24 Sep; stop not guaranteed). Raise a Direct Debit Guarantee indemnity claim for the 23 Sep £875 collected after the 31 Aug tenancy end; decline to raise one for 24 Aug (collected during active tenancy, no error identified). Register a complaint covering the fee and collections. Ask the customer whether she received advance notices for the 23 and 28 Sep collections. No refund, stop or fee reversal is confirmed.

facts.claim: Customer passed ID&V on the personal banking phone call and is the account holder of the payer account.
Direct Debit mandate H&V COLLECT / OAKFIELD PM (ref OPM-78COOMBE-3312) has been active since Feb 2025, monthly £875; the account has no arranged overdraft.
£875 was collected on 24 Aug 2026 and £875 on 23 Sep 2026; the 23 Sep collection took the balance to −£412.90 and a £6.50 unarranged overdraft daily fee was applied on 24 Sep.
A £2,525.00 collection narrated 'FINAL ACCOUNT 78 COOMBE RD' is scheduled for 28 Sep 2026; the instruction was received by the bank 2026-09-24T02:10:44Z and is in status 'scheduled'.
The agency's own email dated 1 Sep 2026 confirms the tenancy at 78 Coombe Road ended on 31 Aug 2026, with the check-out report and deposit still to follow.
The bank cannot see whether advance notices were sent for the September collections; the customer has not yet said whether she received any.
After a £1,019.40 transfer from savings on 25 Sep the available balance is £600.00, less than the £2,525 scheduled collection.
The customer states the agency told her the collection is 'already submitted' and cannot be cancelled on their side; this is a customer-reported statement, not a bank record.
The customer requests refunds of the August and September collections, stopping Monday's collection and reversal of the overdraft fee, stating the fee is not her fault.

missing: Whether the customer received advance notice from Oakfield PM for the 23 Sep £875 and 28 Sep £2,525 collections (bank cannot see originator notices)
Whether the 28 Sep collection can still be stopped/returned by the bank or is already in flight (payments team outcome)
Any specific error the customer alleges in the 24 Aug £875 collection (it fell within the active tenancy)
Outcome of the Direct Debit indemnity claim for the 23 Sep collection and of the complaint review, including any fee decision
What the agency's £2,525 'final account' comprises (a matter between customer and agency, not visible to the bank)

steps.instruction: On the ID&V-passed instruction of account holder Gabriela Petrova (phone, 25 Sep 2026), cancel Direct Debit mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312 (originator OAKFIELD PROPERTY MANAGEMENT LTD, SUN H&V COLLECT 771902) effective immediately, and stop/return unpaid the scheduled collection of £2,525.00 dated 2026-09-28 (received 2026-09-24T02:10:44Z, status 'scheduled'). Report back whether the collection was stopped before processing or is already in flight and will debit.

rationale.explanation: The customer has explicitly instructed that Monday's collection be stopped; she is verified and is the payer. The instruction was received 24 Sep, so a stop is possible but not certain and must be reported, not assumed.
rationale.criterion: A payer can cancel a Direct Debit with their bank; an already-received collection may be in flight, so cancellation must not be promised as certain.

steps.target: Payments / Direct Debit operations team (Harrow & Vale Bank plc)

steps.instruction: Ask: 'Did Oakfield PM send you any advance notice (letter or email) before the £875 taken on 23 September or the £2,525 due on Monday 28 September? If so, when, and what amount and date did it state?'

rationale.explanation: The bank cannot see originator advance notices; whether notice was given and matched the collection is the key fact for the Guarantee error basis on both September collections.
rationale.criterion: A Guarantee claim should identify the error (e.g. no/incorrect advance notice, wrong amount or date) rather than treat every supplier dispute as a refundable error.

steps.instruction: Raise a Direct Debit Guarantee indemnity claim for the collection of £875.00 on 2026-09-23 under mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312 (OAKFIELD PROPERTY MANAGEMENT LTD). Basis: the customer disputes the collection as not due; the originator's own email of 1 Sep 2026 confirms the tenancy at 78 Coombe Road ended 31 Aug 2026; the bank cannot see whether advance notice was sent. Attach agency_move_out_confirmation.eml and statement_extract.csv; add the customer's answer on advance notice when received. Also note the £2,525 collection due 28 Sep so a further claim can be raised if it debits despite s1. Record the outcome; no refund is confirmed.

rationale.explanation: The 23 Sep collection post-dates the tenancy end confirmed by the originator, giving a specific, evidenced basis for a claim; the claims team assesses it rather than the planner deciding eligibility.
rationale.criterion: Keep the Guarantee claim for a collected payment separate from cancelling future instructions; identify the error and route without promising a refund.

steps.target: Direct Debit indemnity claims team (Harrow & Vale Bank plc)

steps.instruction: Decline, on current evidence, to raise a Guarantee claim for the £875.00 collected on 2026-08-24. Reason: it was taken under the regular monthly mandate active since Feb 2025 while the tenancy was still running (ended 31 Aug), and no error in amount, date or notice has been identified. Tell the customer that if she believes a specific error occurred with that collection (e.g. amount differed from notice, or rent already paid), she can tell us and it will be reviewed.

rationale.explanation: The August collection falls within the tenancy period confirmed by the agency and matches the established monthly pattern; refund demands for amounts that appear contractually due are a matter with the supplier, not a scheme error.
rationale.criterion: The Direct Debit Guarantee addresses errors in setup/collection; it is not a universal refund rule for disputes with a supplier.

steps.instruction: Register a complaint for Gabriela Petrova (personal current account) with scope: (a) £875 Direct Debit collected 23 Sep 2026 after her tenancy ended 31 Aug 2026, taking the account £412.90 overdrawn; (b) £6.50 unarranged overdraft daily fee applied 24 Sep which she says is not her fault; (c) £2,525 'final account' collection scheduled 28 Sep. Remedy sought: refund of the Aug and Sep collections, stop of the 28 Sep collection, reversal of the £6.50 fee. Include chronology from statement_extract.csv, the agency email and the incoming instruction, and cross-reference the s1 cancellation request and s3 indemnity claim. Provide the complaint reference and acknowledgement to the customer when issued; the fee decision is for this review.

rationale.explanation: The customer expresses dissatisfaction and demands redress including a fee reversal; this must be registered as a complaint and reviewed separately from the operational cancellation and claim, with no outcome promised.
rationale.criterion: Handle the complaint and the operational query as separate work; a review request does not establish a fee reversal or compensation.

steps.instruction: Tell her: 'I've requested cancellation of the Oakfield PM Direct Debit and asked our payments team to stop Monday's £2,525 collection. Because the agency's instruction reached us on 24 September it may already be in process, so I can't promise it won't debit; if it does, we can raise a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for it. For the £875 taken on 23 September, I've asked our claims team to raise a Guarantee claim because the agency's own email confirms your tenancy ended on 31 August — the outcome is pending, not confirmed. The £875 on 24 August was taken while your tenancy was still running under the usual monthly arrangement, so I can't see an error to claim on — if you think something specific was wrong with it, tell me and we'll look at it. I've asked for a complaint to be registered about the September collection and the £6.50 fee; the fee will be considered in that review and you'll get a reference once it's logged. If you're unhappy with our final answer you can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service. Stopping the Direct Debit doesn't settle whatever the agency says you owe on their final account — that's between you and them. Finally, did you receive any advance notice from Oakfield for the 23 or 28 September collections?' Do not state any action as completed.

rationale.explanation: The customer needs the recorded position on each of her four requests, what remains unconfirmed, and the one missing fact we need from her.
rationale.criterion: Reply with the recorded status and what it does not confirm; do not promise outcomes without evidence.

must_state: Cancellation of the Oakfield PM Direct Debit and a stop/return of Monday's £2,525 collection have been requested; because the instruction reached the bank on 24 Sep it may still be collected, and if it is, a Guarantee claim can be raised for it
A Direct Debit Guarantee indemnity claim for the 23 Sep £875 has been requested on the basis that the tenancy ended 31 Aug per the agency's own email; the outcome is pending

The 24 Aug £875 was collected while the tenancy was still running under the normal monthly mandate, so no error is identified for a Guarantee claim; she can tell us if she believes a specific error occurred

A complaint about the 23 Sep collection and the £6.50 fee has been requested for registration; the fee decision follows the complaint review; if unresolved she can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service
Whether any money is actually owed to Oakfield PM (e.g. the 'final account') remains between her and the agency; stopping the Direct Debit does not settle that
We need to know whether she received advance notices for the 23 Sep and 28 Sep collections
must_not: Promise that the 28 Sep £2,525 collection will definitely be stopped — the instruction was received 24 Sep and may already be in flight
Promise or imply that the September or August £875 will be refunded, or that the £6.50 fee will be reversed, before the indemnity claim and complaint outcomes are recorded
State that August's collection was an error or has been refunded — it was collected on 24 Aug during the active tenancy and no error is identified
Claim that cancelling the mandate reverses collected payments, clears any sum the agency claims, or ends the tenancy/final-account dispute
State that advance notices were or were not sent — the bank cannot see this
Quote a fixed complaint response deadline or predict an Ombudsman outcome
Describe any team action as executed — all are proposals pending execution
